correctness.rationale: The proof closes all induction steps. The maximal \(T\) exists; its central enlargement \(D\) would extend each admissible subgroup by a finite abelian quotient and hence contradict maximality; \(A\) is \(T\)-coset-saturated; every nonidentity fixed-point centralizer lifts to a proper subgroup \(L\); induction gives the needed fixed-point divisibility; Burnside counting isolates the identity term. The pi-separable class satisfies the three hypotheses by standard normal-series arguments.

value.rationale: The result identifies the structural closure principle behind a recent element-solubilizer divisibility theorem and immediately transfers it to the standard pi-separable/p-solvable hierarchy, where generated subgroups need not be soluble. It also pinpoints why fixed derived-length variants can fail: that bounded class is not extension-closed. This is a reusable finite-group lemma rather than a parameter-only or computational variant.
